record.title: Aleph Alpha releases Kolibri, German-English open-weight model
record.summary: Aleph Alpha says Kolibri became publicly available on 3 October 2026 as a downloadable Apache 2.0 model focused on German and English. Its model card describes a mixture-of-experts model with 78.1 billion total parameters and 3.46 billion active per token, 1,048,576-token extended context, and a recommendation to use no more than 262,144 tokens for serving efficiency and complex tasks. The company publishes model weights, a technical report and deployment instructions. Performance, serving-cost advantages, compliance sufficiency and sovereignty outcomes remain provider claims; this review did not independently evaluate them.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: Aleph Alpha announced that Kolibri had been publicly available since 3 October 2026 and linked its downloadable weights, technical report and model documentation.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Aleph Alpha’s model card describes Kolibri as a German-English mixture-of-experts model with 78,103,074,560 total parameters, 3,457,573,120 active parameters per token, Apache 2.0 licensing and a 1,048,576-token extended context; it recommends at most 262,144 tokens for efficient serving and complex tasks.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent matched evaluation of Kolibri’s task performance or serving cost was established in this review.

brief.importance_rationale: If the release characteristics hold, a downloadable German-English model expands the open deployment options for regional-language workloads. This is meaningful but not field-shaping: capability, cost and compliance advantages remain provider-reported and no independent matched evaluation was established.
limitations: Performance, Pareto position, compliance, sovereignty outcomes and customer impact are vendor-reported and were not independently established.
The 1,048,576-token extended context is distinct from the model card’s recommendation of at most 262,144 tokens for serving efficiency and complex tasks.
This review did not download or run the weights, reproduce evaluation results, or inspect customer deployments.

technical.claimed_result: Aleph Alpha describes Kolibri as a German-English reasoning model with tool calling and long-context support. Its model card lists 78,103,074,560 total parameters, 3,457,573,120 active per token, Apache 2.0 licensing and a 1,048,576-token extended context.
technical.demonstrated_result: Aleph Alpha announced public availability from 3 October 2026 and publishes a downloadable model card, weights and deployment instructions. These demonstrate the release and documentation, not the provider’s performance claims.
technical.implementation_status: The weights and supporting documentation are publicly listed on Hugging Face under Apache 2.0. No independent serving run or customer deployment was inspected.
technical.mechanism: The model card describes a mixture-of-experts architecture that activates a subset of parameters per token and provides reasoning and tool-calling modes.
technical.regime: A vendor-released model focused on German and English. The model card recommends context lengths up to 262,144 tokens for efficient serving and complex tasks, despite listing an extended context of 1,048,576 tokens.
technical.reproducibility: The weights, model card and technical report are publicly linked. This review verified the release listing and reported specifications but did not download or run the model or reproduce evaluations.
technical.strongest_baseline: No matched independent baseline was evaluated in this source review.

brief.title: Aleph Alpha releases Kolibri, German-English open-weight model
brief.why_it_matters: A released, downloadable German-English model gives researchers and organizations another option to inspect and deploy under the published license. The source establishes the release and documented model characteristics, but does not establish that the model is competitive, cheaper in practice, compliant for a particular use, or sovereign in operational outcomes.
